subject: Feedback on my first shiny app: fantasy football draft optimizer

messages.author: 2f41c1764121050d
messages.subject: Feedback on my first shiny app: fantasy football draft optimizer
parts:
Hi everyone,

I just created my first Shiny App, and I'm looking for feedback, ideas, and suggestions for improving it.  It's an app designed for optimizing one's draft in fantasy football by maximizing the starting lineup's projected points.

Here is the link to the shiny app:
http://spark.rstudio.com/dadrivr/FantasyFootballDraftOptimizer/

Here is the accompanying blog post:
http://fantasyfootballanalyticsr.blogspot.com/

Thanks, and looking forward to your comments.
-Isaac

messages.author: fa8b9dad524607ca
messages.subject: Re: Feedback on my first shiny app: fantasy football draft optimizer
parts:
Fun stuff- combines my love of football (go Ravens! Born and raised Baltimorean) with shiny.  I have never actually used a cap in any of my leagues, and I suspect a modified version could be useful for such leagues, in a version like Joe mentioned, it would cut down the research/decision time needed when the the guy you wanted and the backup selection that you had in mind just in case get nabbed the two picks ahead of you.  Perhaps a real time suggestion list (or table with projected stats) could be generated after each team's pick?  It may not always be the best available player that you want to select in a given round, if the next half a dozen players at his position aren't much different than him, you can afford to select another player at another position where the value may not hold up until your next selection.  How to calculate any of that I have no idea, I just wing it on draft day, heh.

Does the app take the players bye weeks into consideration?  I tend to prefer players with bye weeks later in the season, for example.  Also, the dreaded suicide backup week is a good thing to avoid.

Tangent- personally I migrated my leagues from yahoo to fleaflicker, and have rather enjoyed the change.

In any event, good work, Isaac!

I'm not that familiar with fantasy football but presumably a user would have a set of selected players who
would be matched with various plays touchdown , sack etc each week each of which would have a specific value
How would Shiny best set up, retain and retrieve these players/values on demand - rather than input them each week
Obviously this could apply to many other uses e.g. stocks by user for a portfolio
andrew clark

messages.subject: Re: Feedback on my first shiny app: fantasy football draft optimizer
parts:
Hmmm, I suppose it would depend quite heavily on the design of the API you're calling (for example, do they give snapshots or historical data).

Personally I would be in favor of having a separate R process that populates your data (maybe in a database or at least .csv files) and then the Shiny app would just poll for changes to the database/file. I'm finishing up some Shiny features to make this (the latter) much easier to do.

messages.author: 2f41c1764121050d
messages.subject: Re: Feedback on my first shiny app: fantasy football draft optimizer
parts:
Thanks for the feedback, guys.  In response to your questions/ideas:

Mike, is your league a snake draft?  If so, I'm planning to write another app for snake drafts.  I'll make sure to include a table of projected points, value, and risk for various players at different positions.  This shiny app was designed for auction drafts (which have a cap).  The app doesn't take bye weeks into consideration, but it would feasible to do so.  I don't know if there is a consensus around the best bye weeks to have.

Joe, that's a very interesting idea about the realtime projected points as games are played.  I'm looking forward to hearing about the upcoming Shiny features for checking for updated data sets.

Thanks!
-Isaac

messages.author: fa8b9dad524607ca
messages.subject: Re: Feedback on my first shiny app: fantasy football draft optimizer
parts:
Aye, it is a snake draft.  And I don't believe there is any consensus for best bye weeks- that's just been a little trick of mine which has helped me win a few championships ;).  But it is fairly common for people to avoid drafting a team which would result in an abundance of players on a bye week at the same time, especially WRs and RBs- and having a backup player with the same bye week as a starter- especially in the one option positions (typically QB, TE, K, DEF), is downright useless.

Thanks!
Mike
